page: Amazon Web Services i2.8xlarge is a storage-optimized second-generation server instance. It is powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2670 v2 processor with 16 physical cores and 32 vCPUs running at 2.5 GHz. The instance features 244.0 GB of system memory, providing 7.62 GB per core. Local storage is a key feature, consisting of 6400 GB of NVMe SSD capacity. Network connectivity is supported by a 10 Gbps baseline bandwidth.

Benchmark data shows average multi-core performance, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 5071.0 and a stress-ng multi-core CPU performance of 27789.21. Single-core performance is relatively weak, as indicated by a Geekbench single-core score of 534.0 and a poor bzip3 single-threaded decompression speed of 7.4 GB/sec. Memory bandwidth is average, reaching 1139.29 GB/sec for small cached blocks and dropping to 82.93 GB/sec for large uncached blocks. Database operations are solid, with Redis SET operations achieving 11.15 million operations per second and Passmark database operations scoring 12597.61.

The i2.8xlarge offers high local storage density and memory capacity, making it qualitatively cost-efficient for workloads requiring large-scale local data caching and high-throughput database operations. However, the older Intel Xeon architecture lacks modern instruction sets like AVX-512, which limits its efficiency in advanced vector calculations and large language model inference, where 70B model prompt processing drops to a poor 3.6 tokens per second. This server is best suited for relational databases, NoSQL databases, transactional processing, and static web serving.
